source.author: verg
source.text: Esto: aegram nulli quondam flexere mariti, non Libyae, non ante Tyro; despectus Iarbas ductoresque alii, quos Africa terra triumphis dives alit: placitone etiam pugnabis amori?
source.text_original: Esto: aegram nulli quondam flexere mariti, / non Libyae, non ante Tyro; despectus Iarbas / ductoresque alii, quos Africa terra triumphis / dives alit: placitone etiam pugnabis amori?
source.text_english: Granted: no husbands at any time bent the sick woman, neither in Libya nor before in Tyre; Iarbas was scorned, and the other princes whom Africa, rich in triumphs, nourishes. Will you also fight against love that is to your liking?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: stringam breuiter reginam Carthaginis, quae magis ardere uoluit quam Iarbae regi nubere, et Hasdrubalis uxorem, quae apprehensis utraque manu liberis in subiectum se praecipitauit incendium, ne pudicitiae damna sentiret, et Lucretiam, quae amissa gloria castitatis noluit pollutae conscientiae superuiuere.
reuse.text_original: stringam breuiter reginam Carthaginis, quae magis ardere uoluit quam Iarbae regi nubere, et Hasdrubalis uxorem, quae apprehensis utraque manu liberis in subiectum se praecipitauit incendium, ne pudicitiae damna sentiret, et Lucretiam, quae amissa gloria castitatis noluit pollutae conscientiae superuiuere.
reuse.text_english: I will briefly mention the queen of Carthage, who preferred to burn rather than marry king Iarbas; and Hasdrubal’s wife, who, seizing her children with both hands, hurled herself into the fire beneath her, so as not to suffer the loss of chastity; and Lucretia, who, when the glory of her chastity was lost, did not wish to survive with a defiled conscience.
